issues.text: Section 4 told me `sub` is Keycloak's id for the user, but here `nameType` is said to tell the identity 'which claim holds the caller's name', and it is given `sub`. I stopped: is `sub` a name or an id? I guessed 'name' here means the claim that identifies the caller, but the lesson does not say so.
issues.quote: It passes the same pair as `nameType` and `roleType`, which tell the identity which claim holds the caller's name and which holds roles
issues.fix: Add a few words after 'the caller's name': 'here the id in `sub`, since Keycloak's token identifies the user by that id'.

issues.text: I had to re-read this sentence twice: 'give some well-known names … longer claim types of its own' made me unsure whether the names or the claim types belong to ASP.NET Core.
issues.quote: Left on, it would give some well-known names, `sub` among them, longer claim types of its own
issues.fix: Reword to: 'Left on, it would rename some well-known claims, `sub` among them, to longer claim types of ASP.NET Core's own'.
